bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : PNG service reaches Buxar's Dumraon, beneficiaries count benefits of piped cooking gas
bihar_raw_news.content: Related News Bihar: PNG service reaches Buxar's Dumraon, beneficiaries count benefits of piped c... Electronics emerges as India`s 'new oil' as trade deficit nears $40 billion Nagaland has potential to emerge as major producer of premium coffee: Governor Centre asks states to help in speeding up switch from LPG to PNG by households Russian crude imports increase to 41 pc, supply secured till July: BPCL Domestic LPG supply normal, 4.58 lakh new PNG connections gasified 2026-10-25 09:07:19 am | Source: IANS Bihar: PNG service reaches Buxar's Dumraon, beneficiaries count benefits of piped cooking gas News By Tags | #Industry #Commodity #Bihar #CookingGas #Dumraon #PNG #AnkitKumar #IndianOil The residents of Dumraon in Buxar district of Bihar are a happy lot as they have received a Diwali bonanza ahead of the festive celebrations. The Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connection has reached their village, giving them an opportunity for uninterrupted cooking gas supply while removing daily hassles of booking LPG cylinders, managing deliveries and also the physical effort of transporting them to respective households. The PNG service was unveiled in the Textile Colony of Dumraon by the District Magistrate. Under the new system, gas will be supplied directly to household kitchens via pipeline. Plans are also in place to expand this service to Buxar city and other areas in the near future. The introduction of prepaid PNG service in the Textile Colony of Dumraon offers consumers an alternative, reducing their reliance on traditional gas cylinders. The facility was inaugurated by District Magistrate Sahila Heer. On this occasion, District Magistrate Sahila Heer mentioned that PNG service would be expanded to other parts of the district. The initiative aims to extend the pipeline network to Buxar city as well as various rural areas in the near future. ''First of all, I would like to congratulate all the IOCL representatives for installing PNG connections here in record time. A total of 498 technically feasible households have been provided with PNG connections, and today, we have inaugurated the service at one household,” the DM Sahila Heer said. Ankit Kumar, Senior Manager (CGD) at Indian Oil , and a resident, Pooja Jha, also shared their perspectives on the new facility. “We have provided connections to five households here, and we plan to supply gas through pipelines to all technically feasible households in Dumraon that meet PNGRB standards in the coming days,'' he stated. The beneficiaries noted that the PNG connection ensures a direct supply of gas to their kitchens, offering greater convenience. They described it as both a practical and cost-effective option. The direct delivery of a piped gas connection offers consumers many conveniences and comforts that existed never before. bihar_raw_news.title: NICDC launches Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited, signs 12 MoUs worth Rs ...
bihar_raw_news.content: NICDC launches Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited, signs 12 MoUs worth Rs 4,200 crore ANI | Updated: Oct 25, 2026 08:09 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 25 (ANI): The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) has launched Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited (BIMCGL), signing 12 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) covering approximately 300 acres of land with proposed investments worth Rs 4,200 crore at Integrated Manufacturing City (IMC) Gaya, as per a statement by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry. The company was formally launched by Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary at Bodh Gaya on Saturday. The event also witnessed the curtain raiser for Bihar Business Connect 2027, the Ministry said. According to the release, BIMCGL is the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) tasked with implementing the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at Gaya under the Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC), part of the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP). “The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) marked a significant milestone in advancing industrial development in Bihar with the formal launch of Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited (BIMCGL) by the Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary, at Bodh Gaya,” the release said. Spread across 1,670 acres in the Dobhi block of Gaya district, the project was approved by the Centre on August 28, 2024, at a total cost of Rs 1,339 crore, including land acquisition costs. “It is expected to attract investments of approximately Rs 16,500 crore and generate employment opportunities for around 1.10 lakh people,” the release said. Incorporated on January 6, 2025, BIMCGL is a joint venture between the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) and the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT), with both holding equal equity stakes. “As the dedicated implementing agency, BIMCGL will expedite project execution through coordinated planning, infrastructure development, statutory clearances, utility connectivity and investor facilitation,” the Ministry said, adding, “The institutional framework will enable faster decision-making, effective monitoring and timely resolution of implementation-related issues.” Infrastructure development at IMC Gaya is underway, with the Bihar government taking possession of the entire project land. The Centre released the first equity tranche of Rs 132 crore in September 2025 against the transfer of 415 acres. Project management consultants and an EPC contractor for trunk infrastructure works have been appointed, while physical construction has commenced. Construction of a dedicated helipad at IMC Gaya is also at an advanced stage to improve accessibility for investors, business delegations and senior officials. The industrial cluster will feature integrated infrastructure, including roads, water supply, sewerage and wastewater treatment facilities, power distribution, solid waste management and fire safety systems. Located near NH-22 and NH-19, with Gaya Airport approximately 39 km away, the project offers connectivity to major industrial and commercial centres. Furthermore, “IMC Gaya will focus on sectors including agro-based industries, textiles and readymade garments, furniture, handicrafts and handloom, and engineering and fabrication. The planned infrastructure will support large manufacturers and MSMEs, encourage local entrepreneurship and strengthen industrial value chains across the region,”

national_raw_news.title: ‘India expresses global sentiment when it urges that dialogue and diplomacy are only soluti...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has said that India expresses global sentiment when it urges that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution for conflicts. He said, India is making efforts itself and is open to working with other partners to that end. Speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan this morning in New Delhi, Dr Jaishankar said, there are two major conflicts going on today in the world in Ukraine and in West Asia. He said, societies and economies, peoples far away, who have little say in the matter, are actually paying the cost. Dr Jaishankar underlined that terrorism is another deadly threat to peace. He said, its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable, it can never be justified and can never be rationalized. The Minister pointed out that terrorism continues because not all states really display zero tolerance. He expressed concern that despite history holding so many lessons, some states still allow political calculations to take precedence. Dr Jaishankar said, the world must therefore develop sharper awareness about this common threat and must come together with stronger resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. He said, progress and prosperity are the flip side of conflict and violence and they too are equally indivisible. The Minister said, the world cannot advance half prosperous and half denied in an era of intricate supply chains, of globalized markets, and of common resources. He said, this is simply a prescription for continuous instability. The Minister said, the Global South today faces a 4F crisis of finance, fuel, food, and fertilizer. He said, the Global North must realize that it has equal stakes in finding solutions. Dr Jaishankar said, the international economy must be urgently de-risked and nations provided with more diversified options. He said, market distortions through constriction and choke points only add to suffering. He added that a genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue. Dr Jaishankar said, progress is understandably associated with the march of technology and humankind now really stands at the crossroads. He said, AI promises to be the mother of all change, but something so sweeping and consequential cannot be left in the hands of just a few. The External Affairs Minister further stated that it will go counter to the trends of freedom and democratization that the world has seen over the last 80 years. He said, for this reason, India is a strong advocate of a responsible, inclusive, and human-centric approach. He added that it is a recognition of AI’s universal applicability and of the need to develop a wider perspective.

national_raw_news.title: India slams Pakistan at UN on Minority Rights Violations and Military Control
national_raw_news.content: India criticised Pakistan at the United Nations, accusing Islamabad of attempting to malign New Delhi through propaganda while diverting attention from its domestic challenges, including economic distress, lawlessness and human rights violations. Speaking during an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Minority Issues at the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee yesterday, India’s First Secretary to the UN, Raghoo Puri, questioned Pakistan’s record on minority rights and alleged that the country’s military continued to exercise decisive control over its political leadership. Referring to the controversy surrounding Pakistan’s 2024 general elections, Puri described Islamabad’s administration as a ‘Form 47 government’ and said it could not override the instructions of the Pakistani military, which he called the country’s ‘real rulers’. Form 47 is an official election document in Pakistan that records the provisional, consolidated results of voting in a constituency. Puri also highlighted concerns over the shrinking minority population in Pakistan and urged Islamabad to focus on the welfare of its own citizens rather than criticising India at international forums. Rejecting Pakistan’s claims on Jammu and Kashmir, he reiterated that the region was an integral part of India and said the outstanding issue was the vacation of territories under Pakistan’s illegal occupation. Defending India’s record on minority rights, Puri described the country as a multi-religious, multi-ethnic and multilingual society, highlighting constitutional safeguards and the contributions of minority communities across government, the armed forces, industry and culture. Puri also stressed that protecting minority rights was primarily the sovereign responsibility of individual countries.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said Mann Ki Baat has completed 12 years and that the journey has felt like a pilgrimage for him. Addressing the nation through his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani, the Prime Minister noted that Mann Ki Baat began on the auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami 12 years ago. Since then, this journey has continued without a break. The Prime Minister said that the listeners of Mann Ki Baat are both his fellow travellers and guides. He further said that Mann Ki Baat has been an auspicious opportunity to proudly celebrate the hard work, valour, commitment, dedication, and spirit of service of the common people of the nation. Mr. Modi added that this has been like a Teerth Yatra (pilgrimage trip) to closely understand the efforts of the people and to salute their contributions. He said people who live for society and the nation are, in themselves, like a ‘Teerth’ (Pilgrimage). He also said that through Mann Ki Baat, he is paying obeisance to the collective strength of the people of India. The Prime Minister said that Mann Ki Baat provides him with an opportunity to connect with every family across the country. He said this deep connection and the affection shown by all of the listeners is a priceless treasure. Saying that the nation possesses many traditional skills that have been a part of its identity for generations, Prime Minister Modi highlighted an initiative underway in Punjab. An organisation called ‘Kheti Virasat Mission’ has begun to breathe new life into organic farming and traditional agricultural practices. The team aimed to promote natural cotton cultivation in the Malwa region of Punjab, with the initiative named ‘Nav-Trinjan’. Under this project, organic cotton with natural colours is cultivated, eliminating the need for additional chemicals to dye the resulting yarn or fabric. ‘Nav-Trinjan’ also established a weaving school with the goal of passing on the craft of weaving to the next generation. Mr Modi mentioned how Ramandeep Kaur, a labourer; Suneha Devi, a domestic help and Rajni Kaur, a manual labourer are now being recognised as a skilled- weavers who are supporting their households with this new found skill. He also mentioned that a shawl woven by Rekha Rani has been presented to the President of India. He recalled meeting this team on National Handloom Day a few months ago. He extended his heartfelt wishes to the entire team for a bright future. Speaking about conservation of Nature, Mr Modi highlighted the efforts in Tehri Garhwal region of Uttarakhand to breathe new life into the ‘Heval’ river and the natural water sources in the surrounding area. He commended the local administration and the villagers who launched a campaign to save the Heval river. Measures were undertaken to capture rainwater, facilitate groundwater recharge and plant a large number of trees. Mr Modi noted with satisfaction that due to these efforts, the Heval river has been revitalised and dozens of natural water sources have received help in their restoration. The Prime Minister noted that cleanliness drives are being run at many places ahead of festivals like Diwali and Chhath. He stressed the need to maintain cleanliness of the places where people live. He added that small, individual efforts can bring about significant change in the surroundings.The Prime Minister expressed happiness that people are placing great importance on Swadeshi products while shopping during this festive season. He remarked that this spirit of ‘Vocal for Local’ is taking Indian products to global markets. He highlighted that Makhana from Purnia in Bihar is now reaching Greece, and Arhar Dal from Kalaburagi in Karnataka is being exported to the Maldives. He underlined that new global markets are opening up for Indian farmers. Mr Modi emphasised that packaging of a product is just as significant as its quality. He cited the example of tribal communities in Maharashtra who have placed a strong focus on the packaging of the products they create. Through an initiative called ‘Shabari Naturals,’ products like honey, mahua, chironji and bamboo-based items are being brought to the market with packaging which reflects their tribal art. Mr Modi shared that this packaging has received Japan’s prestigious ‘Good Design Award.’ Prime Minister Modi also spoke...

national_raw_news.title: Low-pressure system over Bay of Bengal likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam 4 hours ago 59
national_raw_news.content: The Low-pressure system over Bay of Bengal likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115 to 125 kilometres per hour gusting to 140 kilometres per hour by forenoon of Wednesday. India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday and Wednesday and also over Odisha and Telangana on Wednesday. The India Meteorological Department has issued a pre-cyclone watch for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts, as a depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm. The IMD has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh on October 27 and 28. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain alert and warn people in low-lying areas. Fisheries officials are taking steps to bring fishing boats safely ashore. Power utilities are also preparing teams to restore electricity in case of disruptions. Odisha is on alert for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, strong winds and possible flooding, as the state government steps up disaster preparedness. Akashvani correspondent reports that the Met Dept is closely monitoring a depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal, which is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and a severe cyclonic storm by day after tomorrow. It may further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before approaching the Andhra Pradesh coast around Wednesday morning. The system was located about 860 kilometres east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 1,130 kilometres east of Bapatla in the latest bulletin from IMD. The projected landfall zone is along the Andhra Pradesh coast, between Visakhapatnam and Bapatla, though the precise location remains subject to further updates. Odisha is likely to experience heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several districts under the impact of the weather system. The state government has placed all districts on alert and kept disaster-response teams on standby. Fishermen have been advised to return to shore and avoid venturing into the sea. People are urged to follow official weather advisories.

national_raw_news.title: Centre achieves target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs across the country
national_raw_news.content: The Centre has created 11 crore farmer IDs across the country, five months ahead of the March 2027 deadline. The milestone has been achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The Farmer ID initiative is designed to provide farmers with a unique digital identity, enabling transparent, efficient and timely access to government schemes, bank credit, crop insurance and disaster relief, while reducing paperwork and repeated verification. Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said this today while sharing a video message. The Minister said that the target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs by March 2027 was set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and it was achieved yesterday, five months ahead of schedule. Mr Chouhan said that Farmer IDs will ensure transparent delivery of benefits under various government schemes. They will facilitate farmers in accessing bank loans, crop insurance, disaster relief assistance and selling their produce. He added that the initiative will help ensure that benefits reach the right farmers, while the use of modern technology will make farming easier and more efficient. Mr Chouhan congratulated and thanked the officials and employees of the Central Government, as well as the state governments, union territories, and district administrations, for this achievement. The Ministry added that the Digital Agriculture Mission was launched following the Union Cabinet’s approval on 2nd September, 2024. The Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) being developed under the mission is already showing results on the ground. It added that through the Farmer ID-based service delivery system, more than 6 crore farmers across the country have so far received direct benefits under various schemes. Linking a verified farmer database with agricultural services is helping eliminate fraud and the need for duplicate verification. The Ministry furhter stated that it has also improved coordination among government departments and strengthened policy formulation and the monitoring of schemes, making it easier to track their implementation and delivery of benefits.
